entry.heading: Jacob Metoyer
entry.lead: I study computer science and physics at CSULB. My work connects research, the software I build through HAMON, and the original universe Spire of Octaves.
entry.journeyNote: Research, HAMON, and Spire of Octaves: three ways into my work.

publicBio.name: Jacob Metoyer
publicBio.intro: I study computer science and physics at Cal State Long Beach. My work spans academic and independent research, the software estate HAMON, and the original multimedia universe Spire of Octaves.
publicBio.research: I’m a BUILD Scholar with a biology minor, working toward MD/PhD training. My collaborative research experience spans gait and rehabilitation, behavioral neurobiology, protein molecular dynamics, and surgical ergonomics.
publicBio.interests: I’m interested in neuroscience, movement and behavior, scientific computing, and tools for investigating complex systems.
publicBio.researchLead: I work across academic collaboration and independent investigation. The common thread is using experiments, computation, and models to understand movement, behavior, and complex systems.
publicBio.contactLead: Research, software, or a world worth building?

researchResource.name: CaptureSuite
researchResource.description: Independent research software for collecting multiple streams into sealed sessions. Its public example runs the offline QC workflow on a synthetic package.
researchResource.limit: The example uses metadata and placeholder segments, not measured signal quality or patient data.

researchSections.title: Academic research
researchSections.lead: Collaborative work across biology, movement, and computation.
researchSections.detail: My research experience spans gait and rehabilitation, behavioral neurobiology, protein molecular dynamics, and surgical ergonomics.

researchSections.title: Independent research
researchSections.lead: Questions pursued through custom software and explicit models—including research developed through HAMON.
researchSections.detail: Examples below ask how to distinguish physical models, search for correct and efficient GPU implementations, and update computational memory. Visual-computing and causal-model prototypes offer further investigations.

journeys.title: Enter Spire of Octaves
journeys.lead: A vertical world, an unfinished song, and the people who keep it alive.

steps.body: Spire of Octaves is a setting for stories, games, music, and animation. Seamwork is one entrance: a dangerous guiding job in a world whose seams can be heard and mended.

ending.heading: Enter the wider world
ending.body: Spire has its own home for the universe, its writing, and ways to explore.

journeys.motivation: A world becomes interesting through the people who must live with its rules.

journeys.title: Explore HAMON
journeys.lead: An engineering estate led by Hamon Engine, with applications, tools, and interactive experiments.

steps.prompt: What does it take to build the engine itself?
steps.body: Hamon Engine brings rendering, replayable simulation, animation, physics, content authoring, and programmable control into a custom Rust + wgpu workspace.

steps.prompt: What does a small engine-built world feel like to play?
steps.body: Lanternwake is a public browser snapshot: restore three lanterns on a small island and return to the stone arch at dawn.

ending.heading: Keep exploring the software
ending.body: HAMON also includes research tools, focused applications, and smaller experiments. Public code is collected on GitHub; the engine source remains private.

journeys.motivation: Building the engine means working on how a world behaves, not only what it looks like.

projectStories.question: A world still being composed.
projectStories.opening: Spire of Octaves is my original multimedia universe: cities stacked on cities, shaped by an unfinished sacred song. It is a setting for stories, games, music, and animation.
projectStories.capability: Worldbuilding, language work, character and place design, and multiple writing projects all belong to Spire. Seamwork is a public entrance into that much larger body of work.
projectStories.tryThis: Visit Spire’s own site to explore the wider universe. Seamwork offers one entrance through its writing.
projectStories.limit: Seamwork’s serialization is currently on hiatus.

projectStories.question: The machinery for making worlds.
projectStories.opening: Hamon Engine is a custom Rust + wgpu engine bringing rendering, simulation, content tools, and programmable control into one engineering project.
projectStories.capability: Its maintained workspace includes physically based and stylized rendering, skeletal animation, rigid-body physics, replayable simulation, editable mesh recipes, asset cooking, and CLI, JSON-RPC, and MCP control. These tools make the world itself something you can build, inspect, and change.
projectStories.tryThis: Explore the engine’s systems, then open Lanternwake for a small public playable example.
projectStories.limit: The source remains private. Public browser games are published snapshots, not the whole current engine.

next.label: Explore the creative universe beside the engine

projectStories.question: What is just outside the camera’s view?
projectStories.opening: A video records one camera’s path. Phantom Window lets you explore nearby viewpoints: lean away from the original framing, inspect an edge, and compare what changes.
projectStories.capability: The prototype estimates depth and camera motion, reuses pixels across frames, and renders nearby viewpoints. Source comparison and pixel provenance keep the reconstruction open to inspection.
projectStories.tryThis: Compare camera-left and camera-right, then switch to “Where pixels came from.” Watch the edges of the bird and the newly exposed background.
projectStories.limit: Nearby views contain estimated geometry and inferred regions.

next.label: Another camera problem: reconstruct a basketball play

projectStories.question: What if a caption had a place in the scene?
projectStories.opening: A line can be quiet, shouted, interrupted, or spoken behind someone else. Captionverse explores what changes when those differences affect the presentation of the words.
projectStories.capability: The local-video workbench combines editable subtitles, speaker-linked layouts, experimental depth-aware text, phrase recall, and interval replay. Original subtitles and reviewed revisions stay separate.
projectStories.tryThis: Switch between depth overlap, emphasis, and two speakers. All three examples use the same pop-out style on one licensed film excerpt.
projectStories.limit: Automatic transcription and placement remain drafts to review.

next.label: Look behind the depth: where did those pixels come from?

projectStories.question: Why did the door unlock when nobody was home?
projectStories.opening: A familiar visitor rings. One rule welcomes them; another should protect an empty house. DOMINO makes the resulting event chain small enough to reason about.
projectStories.capability: Replay the modeled observations, inspect rule guards and competing commands, reduce the counterexample, and compare repairs against behavior that should still work.
projectStories.tryThis: Compare the recorded outcomes of changing a delay, disabling the rules, and requiring the resident to be home. Removing a visible conflict is not the same as fixing the case.
projectStories.limit: Invented events and finite model checks; no real-home connection.

next.label: Keep a baseline, then branch a different outcome

projectStories.question: Could you watch the possession from above?
projectStories.opening: A broadcast camera catches the possession as it happens. Replay Forge explores that movement through a navigable court model and lets an alternative play branch beside it.
projectStories.capability: A licensed 19-second basketball excerpt supplies person and ball detections. A calibrated court, free camera, source inset, and saved branches support comparison without overwriting the original.
projectStories.tryThis: Look between the source inset and the overhead court. Keep observed footage, reconstructed motion, and authored alternatives distinct.
projectStories.limit: Tracking is fragmented. Alternate plays are authored, not predictions.

next.label: Another what-if: change a rule and inspect the consequences

projectStories.question: Restore the lights. Return at dawn.
projectStories.opening: Three lanterns give you a reason to cross a small island. Bring them back to life, then find the stone arch as morning arrives.
projectStories.capability: Lanternwake is a public browser game built with Hamon Engine. Its compact loop turns engine work into something you can move through and finish.
projectStories.tryThis: Open the game in a WebGPU-capable browser. Keyboard and on-screen touch controls are available.
projectStories.limit: WebGPU required. This is a published snapshot, not the latest engine build.

recordedRepairChoices.heading: Three ways to change the same case
recordedRepairChoices.intro: A familiar visitor arrives while the resident is away. These are recorded outcomes from DOMINO’s local example, not a live simulation on this page.

choices.label: Delay the welcome by 1 ms
choices.outcome: The command collision disappears. The door still unlocks while the resident is away.

choices.label: Disable every rule
choices.outcome: The defects disappear, but the desired-behavior checks fail too.

choices.label: Require the resident to be home
choices.change: Known visitor → known visitor and resident home
choices.outcome: The observed conflict and away-unlock violation disappear. All 22 stated behavior checks remain satisfied across four modeled contexts.

recordedRepairChoices.limit: Finite, synthetic checks do not establish safe behavior in every future event sequence.

connections.label: Depth changes what you see
connections.description: One moves the viewpoint through a scene; the other experiments with the position of text inside it. Both need to account for occlusion and missing information.

connections.label: One camera, incomplete geometry
connections.description: Both reconstruct a view the source camera did not record. Keeping the original nearby makes the estimate easier to question.

connections.label: Keep the original. Try a branch.
connections.description: An automation repair and an alternate play both become more useful when you can compare them with the unchanged starting case.

connections.label: Separate the record from the interpretation
connections.description: Preserving original subtitles beside reviewed edits echoes a practical concern in research software: retain what was recorded when an interpretation changes.

connections.label: Show the uncertainty
connections.description: The connection is a question about measurement, not a claim of clinical validation: what came from observation, and what came from an estimate?

connections.label: Rules have consequences
connections.description: In the simulator, a rule changes the event chain. In fiction, a world’s rules change what its people can do and what it costs them. The connection is thematic, not a shared implementation.

connections.label: A creative universe and an engineering foundation.
connections.description: Spire of Octaves and Hamon Engine are my two major projects. One develops a world across creative forms; the other develops tools and systems for interactive worlds. They are distinct projects, not a claim of a finished Spire game running on Hamon.

connections.label: A small world you can play.
connections.description: Lanternwake is a public compiled browser snapshot built with Hamon Engine. It is a playable example, not the full engine or its latest source state.

connections.label: Computation that reaches beyond games.
connections.description: Alongside rendering and simulation, the engine workspace contains scientific tools for working with geometry and physical models. My research background gives that work another context.

relatedWork.name: Threadline
relatedWork.question: What did we actually agree to?
relatedWork.description: Review commitments and dependencies beside the exact conversation words. Corrections preserve the history of the interpretation.
relatedWork.limit: Human-reviewed suggestions; no verified live Bee connection.

relatedWork.question: Which memories should this visitor see?
relatedWork.description: Build a local photo story from approved sources, with visitor-specific sharing and deliberate revocation.
relatedWork.limit: Fictional demo family; identity and consent remain keeper-attested.
relatedWork.connectionLabel: Another way to return to a moment.
relatedWork.connectionDescription: Familiar Memories builds photo stories around the people allowed to see them.

relatedWork.name: Threshold
relatedWork.question: What should the door say back?
relatedWork.description: Review an arrival and the exact proposed response before approving it in a local practice workflow.
relatedWork.limit: No message delivery, identity verification, or lock control.
relatedWork.connectionLabel: Before a response becomes an action.
relatedWork.connectionDescription: Threshold makes the proposed reply visible for resident review; DOMINO investigates the rules behind a modeled action.

relatedWork.name: LedgerDock
relatedWork.question: What arrived, and what is still unresolved?
relatedWork.description: Track orders, split shipments, parcel checks, count corrections, returns, and replacements in a local receiving workbench.
relatedWork.limit: Manual records; no automated inspection or multiuser sync.
relatedWork.connectionLabel: Follow an exception through a workflow.
relatedWork.connectionDescription: A parcel count, a replacement, and a return need a legible record of what changed.

relatedWork.name: Teachback
relatedWork.question: Does the same idea still work in a new problem?
relatedWork.description: Explain a quantitative idea, make a prediction, inspect task-specific feedback, and try an authored application or later revisit.
relatedWork.limit: Four authored topics. Writing is not semantically graded; learning gains are unmeasured.
relatedWork.connectionLabel: Turn an explanation into a new question.
relatedWork.connectionDescription: Teachback explores quantitative understanding through authored problems, explicit help, and later revisits.

relatedWork.name: Wild Neighbors
relatedWork.question: How could an observation become part of a living habitat?
relatedWork.description: Prototype components for reviewing wildlife observations, recovering work, and preparing habitat intake.
relatedWork.limit: The habitat integration remains illustrative, not a complete connected product.
relatedWork.connectionLabel: From an observation toward a habitat.
relatedWork.connectionDescription: A separate early software experiment explores the components for a world shaped by reviewed observations; it is not a Spire adaptation.

relatedWork.name: Clearway
relatedWork.question: Which observed conditions meet a spatial rule?
relatedWork.description: Evaluate explicit observer annotations against spatial criteria and inspect the resulting judgments.
relatedWork.limit: Annotation-based evaluation, not camera perception or object detection.
relatedWork.connectionLabel: Another way to ask a spatial question.
relatedWork.connectionDescription: Clearway starts from explicit observer annotations rather than estimating a scene from pixels.

independent.name: WORLDLAW
independent.question: What measurement would distinguish two explanations of the same motion?
independent.output: An executable torque-model workbench that compares candidate explanations, proposes a discriminating measurement, and replays predictions.
independent.detail: The virtual instrument begins with small-angle data that fit both spring and gravity models. A proposed wide-angle measurement changes the selected model to gravity; withheld predictions update. Motion Lab also uses a declared fixed pivot and a tracked video marker to produce angular observations, retaining gaps and corrections.
independent.limit: Finite seven-term scalar torque library; default experiments are synthetic. Video tracking requires declared calibration and does not establish physical laws.

independent.name: Kernel Garden
independent.question: Can a faster implementation survive independent correctness checks?
independent.output: Generate CUDA candidates, compile and measure them on a real GPU, reject incorrect variants, and export the measured winner.
independent.detail: Retained trials cover float32 vector addition on one RTX 4070. Bounded block-size search adds a held-out size; an exported winner was separately compiled and checked with new inputs. A complementary CPU arena explores compiled AXPY variants.
independent.limit: One GPU device and one GPU operator; parameter search, not general algorithm invention or an established speedup over vendor libraries.

independent.name: Computational memory
independent.question: When should a system revise what it remembers?
independent.output: Retrieval-plasticity and consolidation experiments test how records are reweighted and when repeated episodes justify reusable lessons.
independent.detail: Bounded per-record strengths reorder retrieval within fixed trust tiers. A separate consolidation prototype preserves raw records and evaluates proposed lessons on chronological holdouts, retaining conflicting interpretations rather than overwriting them.
independent.limit: Offline and synthetic replays; some mechanisms remained staged at the recorded study checkpoint. Not a biological memory model or an established learning-gain result.
